reels.title: Why is the sky blue?
reels.hook: On the Moon, the sky is black. Even at noon.
reels.caption:
On the Moon, the sky is black. Even at noon. 🌑

Earth's air is the difference. Sunlight holds every color, and air molecules scatter short wavelengths most. Violet (400 nm) scatters about ten times more than deep red (700 nm).

So why isn't the sky violet? Sunlight has less of it, and our eyes are less sensitive to it.

Did you expect violet to win? 👇

Sources: NASA; Royal Museums Greenwich; Physics FAQ.
reels.alt_text: A cut-paper animation. A blue sky is torn open to show an astronaut under a black Moon sky. A sunbeam fans into colored strips, paper molecules scatter them, ten violet cards outnumber one red card, and paper layers turn the sky to sunset.

sources.name: NASA Space Place: Why is the sky blue?

reels.title: Why neon glows
reels.hook: Most neon colors contain no neon at all.
reels.caption:
Most neon colors contain no neon at all. 💡

Neon gas glows reddish-orange. Electricity pushes electrons through the gas, they hit atoms, and the atoms give the energy back as light.

Blue comes from argon with a little mercury, often with a coating too. Many other colors come from powder inside the glass that turns ultraviolet into visible light.

Which sign color would you pick? 👇

Sources: Edison Tech Center; Wikipedia (Neon sign, Neon).
reels.alt_text: An animated neon sign lights up red on a rainy brick wall, then the view goes inside the tube where dots representing electrons and a ring-shaped atom glow. Blue, pink, green and white signs light up in turn, before the neon-free ones switch off.

reels.title: Why is Mercury so hard to reach?
reels.hook: This spacecraft took eight years to reach Mercury.
reels.caption:
Eight years to reach Mercury. 🛰️

The Sun's gravity keeps pulling a spacecraft faster, and go too fast and you can't stop. So BepiColombo swung past Earth once, Venus twice and Mercury six times before entering orbit on November 21, 2026.

A software glitch ended its engine burn early, leaving a 75-hour orbit instead of 58. ESA says no extra burns are needed. The two orbiters are due to separate December 9–10.

Would you have waited eight years? 👇

Sources: ESA; WRAL (NASA Ambassador Tony Rice).
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation. A spacecraft with blue solar panels falls toward a huge yellow Sun, flies past Mercury, then swings by Earth, Venus and Mercury before circling Mercury and splitting into two orbiters.

reels.title: 245 animals in one rock
reels.hook: 245 animals lived in this one rock.
reels.caption:
One deep-sea rock, 245 animals. 🪨

Scientists examined 244 fist-sized nodules from the Pacific seafloor, 4 to 6 km down, and found 4,139 animals. The average was 17 per rock. One held 245.

The rocks grow a few millimeters in a million years, and they're rich in metal.

Mine them or leave them? 👇

Source: Scientific Reports (2026), via MARUM and ScienceDaily.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation of a dark seafloor rock covered in tiny colorful animals, compared with a fist, shown deep in the Pacific, then lifted by a yellow mining claw.

reels.title: How El Niño changes winter
reels.hook: Warm water in one place can bring rain far away.
reels.caption:
Warm water in one place, rain far away. 🌧️

In El Niño, Pacific trade winds weaken and warm water moves back toward the Americas. The jet stream shifts south. The Gulf Coast and Southeast tend wetter, and the northern U.S. tends warmer and drier.

Forecasters put the chance of strong to very strong El Niño lasting through January–March 2027 at roughly 80% (November 19 update). That's odds, not a promise.

What's winter doing where you are? 👇

Sources: NOAA; Drought.gov.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation of the Pacific Ocean: wind arrows weaken, a patch of warm orange water slides east, the jet stream moves south across a schematic U.S. map, and dice land on sixes.

sources.name: NOAA Ocean Service: El Niño and La Niña

reels.title: Same Question, Different World 2: Rain
reels.hook: There is a world where it may rain iron.
reels.caption:
There is a world where it may rain iron. ☄️

On Earth, rain is water. On Titan, at −179 °C, methane makes the rain, rivers and seas. On WASP-76b, winds carry iron vapor to the cooler night side, where astronomers suspect it condenses and falls.

Same Question, Different World, part 2. Part 1: why our sky is blue and the Moon's is black.

Next: sunsets. Which world should we visit? 👇

Sources: NASA; ESO.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation of rain on three worlds: gray iron drops under red clouds, blue water over a person with an umbrella, and pale methane drops over an orange landscape on Saturn's moon Titan.

sources.name: ESO: planet where it rains iron (2020)

reels.title: Is water wet?
reels.hook: Is water wet? Science and the dictionary disagree.
reels.caption:
Is water wet? 💧

In science, wetting is what a liquid does to a surface. By that rule, water makes other things wet.

Dictionaries split. Dictionary.com says wet means moistened, covered or soaked. Wiktionary says it can mean made up of liquid, and by that rule water is wet.

Our verdict: wet is what happens to the dry thing. Team Wet or Team Not Wet? 👇

Sources: USGS; Wikipedia (Wetting); Dictionary.com; Wiktionary.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation. A frowning water drop asks if it is wet. Drops soak a towel, a drop spreads on one surface and beads on another, a dictionary opens, and a verdict reads: wet is what happens to the dry thing.

sources.name: USGS: Adhesion and cohesion of water

reels.title: Same Question, Different World 3: Sunsets
reels.hook: On Mars, the sunset is blue.
reels.caption:
On Mars, the sunset is blue. 🔵

Earth's air scatters blue away, so red gets through. Martian dust is fine enough to let blue through best and keep it near the Sun. Curiosity saw it in color on April 15, 2015.

Uranus here is a NASA simulation. The Moon's sky just stays black.

Same Question, Different World, part 3. Next: snow. Which sunset would you watch? 👇

Sources: NASA; JPL; Royal Museums Greenwich.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation of sunsets: blue rings around a small Sun over red Martian ground with a rover, orange layers on Earth, blue layers for Uranus, and a black Moon sky with an astronaut.

sources.name: NASA: Sunset in Mars' Gale Crater

reels.title: Same Question, Different World 4: Snow
reels.hook: On Mars, snowflakes may be cubes.
reels.caption:
On Mars, snowflakes may be cubes. 🧊

Earth's have six sides because of how water molecules line up. Mars also has dry-ice snow, and its fourfold symmetry means scientists expect tiny cubes. As of 2022, nobody had pictured it falling.

On Enceladus, jets spray ice and most falls back like snow.

Same Question, Different World, part 4. Next: how long is a day? 👇

Sources: NASA JPL; NASA; NOAA.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation: a large ice cube falls on Mars, a six-armed snowflake falls on Earth, carbon dioxide molecules appear, and ice jets spray from Enceladus beside Saturn.

sources.name: NASA JPL: Winter wonderland on Mars (2022)

reels.title: We hit an asteroid. Here's what it did.
reels.hook: We hit an asteroid. Now we've gone back to look.
reels.caption:
We hit an asteroid. Now we've gone back to look. ☄️

On September 26, 2022, NASA's DART hit Dimorphos on purpose and shortened its orbit by 33 minutes. Today ESA's Hera showed what happened: one face flattened into a stadium-sized crater, a wild tumble, and hundreds of boulders flying around the pair. The rest looks unchanged.

ESA calls these first images the beginning. Hera moves in to about 13 km in December.

Which result surprised you? 👇

Source: ESA, November 25, 2026.
reels.alt_text: Cut-paper animation. A gray asteroid is struck by a small spacecraft, its orbit shrinks, the Hera spacecraft arrives, a flattened crater is circled beside a stadium, and boulders circle the tumbling rock.

sources.name: ESA: Hera reveals stadium-sized asteroid crater (Nov 25, 2026)
